videos.title: How Much Independent Data Do You Have?
videos.description:
More rows do not always mean more independent evidence.

In this hands-on LEARN lesson, we work through a reproducible Python example in JupyterLab to see how repeated measurements, group sizes and data splits affect the conclusions we can draw.

You’ll learn how to:
• Distinguish stored rows from independent sampling units.
• Compare uncertainty calculations based on rows and whole cases.
• Detect group leakage and keep training, validation and test cases separate.
• Resample whole cases with the bootstrap.

Code, Jupyter notebooks and materials:
https://github.com/ricardofitas/RFLabs-LEARN/tree/main/season-1/02-how-much-independent-data

Chapters
00:00 More measurements, more independent evidence?
00:41 Choose the independent unit
01:28 Build and check the Python example
03:01 Two standard errors, two assumptions
03:45 Duplicate rows without adding independent cases
04:32 Covariance and effective sample size
06:13 Unequal groups and weighting
06:59 Random row splits and grouped partitions
08:36 Fit preprocessing on training data
09:24 Bootstrap the independent unit
10:09 Hierarchies, time series and the claim you can make
11:38 A practical audit for your own project

The examples use synthetic teaching data.
